title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
authors: Benjamin Scheibehenne; Rainer Greifeneder; Peter M. Todd
finding_paraphrase: Average choice-overload effect was near zero with substantial variation.
applicability_limit: Assortment alone does not establish overload; mixed experimental tasks, not Pepsodent buyers.

title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta‐analysis
authors: Alexander Chernev; Ulf Böckenholt; Joseph Goodman
finding_paraphrase: Choice complexity, task difficulty, uncertain preferences and effort minimization moderated overload.
applicability_limit: Moderators sharpen a test; they do not establish which mechanism drives Indonesian downtrading.

title: An Alternative Explanation for Lower Repeat Rates after Promotion Purchases
authors: Scott A. Neslin; Robert W. Shoemaker
design_population: Formal models, simulation and exploratory empirical analysis
finding_paraphrase: Lower average repeat after a deal can arise from temporary recruitment of low-purchase-probability households.
applicability_limit: Cohort composition is an alternative to a causal damage effect of discounts; verify comparable cohorts.

title: Long-Run Effects of Promotion Depth on New Versus Established Customers: Three Field Studies
authors: Eric T. Anderson; Duncan I. Simester
design_population: Three field experiments;durables sold through direct-mail catalog
finding_paraphrase: Deeper discounts increased subsequent purchasing for first-time customers but reduced it for established customers.
applicability_limit: Counterexample to universal discount pessimism; durables/catalog context is not replenishment toothpaste.

title: Impact of Sales Promotions on when, what, and how Much to Buy
authors: Sunil Gupta
design_population: IRI household scanner panel;regular ground coffee;purchase timing/brand/quantity models
finding_paraphrase: Promotion lift can be separated into brand switching,purchase acceleration and quantity changes.
applicability_limit: Reported coffee-specific proportions cannot be transferred to toothpaste; stockpiling was small in that application.

title: Consumer Promotions and the Acceleration of Product Purchases
authors: Scott A. Neslin; Caroline Henderson; John Quelch
design_population: Analytical framework applied to two product classes
finding_paraphrase: Promotion-related acceleration includes larger quantities and shorter interpurchase times.
applicability_limit: Purchase timing is different from consumption,preference or incremental category demand.

title: Consumer Price and Promotion Expectations: An Experimental Study
authors: Manohar U. Kalwani; Chi Kin Yim
design_population: Controlled experiment;direct elicitation of price expectations
finding_paraphrase: Promotion frequency and discount depth affected expected prices;unexpected absence/presence of deals influenced choice.
applicability_limit: Mechanism support,not proof Pepsodent regular prices are rejected because of reference prices.

title: A Price Expectations Model of Customer Brand Choice
authors: Manohar U. Kalwani; Chi Kin Yim; Heikki J. Rinne; Yoshi Sugita
finding_paraphrase: Expected-price model fit better than a traditional choice model;responses to price losses exceeded gains.
applicability_limit: Observational model fit and category transfer are limited;not a Pepsodent elasticity estimate.

title: Package size and perceived quality: The intervening role of unit price perceptions
authors: Dengfeng Yan; Jaideep Sengupta; Robert S. Wyer
finding_paraphrase: Smaller packs could imply higher quality through higher unit-price perceptions;effect reversed under specified distraction/information conditions.
applicability_limit: Small packs can communicate quality or cost;cannot presume a universal poor-value response.

title: Consumer Response to Package Downsizing: Evidence from the Chicago Ice Cream Market
authors: Metin Çakır; Joseph V. Balagtas
design_population: Household scanner panel;Chicago bulk ice cream;random-utility demand model
finding_paraphrase: Consumers responded less to package-size changes than to price changes in this market.
applicability_limit: No transfer of the reported elasticity ratio to Indonesian toothpaste;downsizing differs from distinct premium packs.

title: The consumer competence of young adults: a study of newly formed households
authors: Alice Grønhøj
design_population: Mixed methods;18–25-year-olds establishing their first household
finding_paraphrase: Family/friend guidance mattered in complex decisions;hypothetical competence exceeded observed decision competence.
applicability_limit: Transition context supports asking actual behavior;does not estimate who funds Indonesian toothpaste.

title: Influence of parents, peers, and media on adolescents' consumer knowledge, attitudes, and purchase behavior: A meta‐analysis
authors: Anubhav Mishra; Moutusy Maity
finding_paraphrase: Parents,peers and media influence consumer socialization;age and cultural context moderate relationships.
applicability_limit: Adolescents are not the complete18–30target;brand influence is not purchase authority or payment.

title: The effectiveness of dentifrices without and with sodium lauryl sulfate on plaque, gingivitis and gingival abrasion--a randomized clinical trial.
authors: Sälzer S, Rosema NA, Martin EC, Slot DE, Timmer CJ, Dörfer CE, van der Weijden GA.
design_population: RCT120 non-dental students18–34 in Amsterdam;116 completed8weeks
finding_paraphrase: No significant between-formulation plaque/bleeding difference;SLS formulation rated higher for taste,freshness and foam.
applicability_limit: No-difference test does not prove universal equivalence;formulations differ beyond a perfectly isolated SLS manipulation.
funding_review: Sara Lee funded ACTA role;coauthor former Sara Lee/current Colgate-Palmolive.

title: The effectiveness of a dentifrice without sodium lauryl sulphate on dental plaque and gingivitis - a randomized controlled clinical trial.
authors: Sälzer S, Rosema N, Hennequin-Hoenderdos NL, Slot DE, Timmer C, Dörfer CE, Van der Weijden GA.
finding_paraphrase: No significant plaque/gingivitis differences;SLS-containing formulations preferred for foam;test non-SLS formulation contained enzymes,colostrum,zinc.
applicability_limit: Not an Enzim-brand trial;not proof more foam cleans better.
funding_review: EuropePMC grant field:Department of Periodontology of ACTA;full disclosure not reviewed.

title: Desensitizing Toothpastes for Dentin Hypersensitivity: A Network Meta-analysis.
authors: Martins CC, Firmino RT, Riva JJ, Ge L, Carrasco-Labra A, Brignardello-Petersen R, Colunga-Lozano LE, Granville-Garcia AF, Costa FO, Yepes-Nuñez JJ, Zhang Y, Schünemann HJ.
finding_paraphrase: Benefits and evidence certainty differed by active ingredient and pain stimulus.
applicability_limit: Clinical ingredient evidence is not brand switching,retention or a justification for Premium for everyone.

title: Formulations of desensitizing toothpastes for dentin hypersensitivity: a scoping review.
authors: Martins CC, Riva JJ, Firmino RT, Schünemann HJ.
finding_paraphrase: Formulations,actives,fluoride and abrasive combinations varied;more product names do not imply interchangeable formulations.
applicability_limit: Ranks formulations using an earlier NMA;not an independent new effectiveness estimate or retention study.
funding_review: See fulltext disclosure;do not infer none from missing API grant field.

title: Effect of desensitizing toothpastes on dentine hypersensitivity: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Hu ML, Zheng G, Zhang YD, Yan X, Li XC, Lin H.
finding_paraphrase: Several desensitizing formulations reduced hypersensitivity relative to negative controls,with varying evidence quality.
applicability_limit: Overlapping primary trials with later reviews;not an independent extra vote;not direct brand comparison.

title: Sensory Investigation of Toothpaste Particle Perception in the Mouth.
authors: Teoman B, Potanin A.
design_population: Sensory panel with rheological,tribological and surface measurements
finding_paraphrase: Instrumental features predicted grittiness/particle-perception ratings in tested pastes.
applicability_limit: Perception-model performance does not establish clinical cleaning or Indonesian consumer preference.

title: Sensory Perception Optimization of Consumer Products: Toothpaste Tube Squeezability.
authors: Teoman B, Vandeven M, Cabelly A, Morelli M, Potanin A.
finding_paraphrase: Acceptability varied with dispensing resistance;both excessive and insufficient resistance can be undesirable.
applicability_limit: Ease of dispensing is a distinct pack experience;not proof small tubes cause faster consumption.

title: Sensory Investigation of Toothpaste Foam Using Rheology and Dynamic Foam Analysis.
authors: Teoman B, Lee J, Mai P, Yu J, Kolle P, Vandeven M, Cabelly A, Morelli M, Potanin A.
design_population: 15custom formulations;instrumental foam analysis linked to sensory panel
finding_paraphrase: Foam characteristics correlated with reported sensory ratings.
applicability_limit: Published Aug2026:post-case contextual evidence;no claim to explain H12026 causes or efficacy.

title: Zero Waste: Consumers' Perception of the Use of Eco-friendly Toothpaste Tablets-A Quasi-experimental Study.
authors: Sandhu J, Calderon B, Park B, Patel J, Garcia-Godoy F, Oyoyo U, Kwon SR.
finding_paraphrase: Sensory acceptance was multidimensional;texture dislike coexisted with favorable responses on other dimensions.
applicability_limit: Novel tablet format and stated intent do not establish clinical efficacy or actual tube-to-tube repurchase.

title: The Effects of Sensory and Nonsensory Factors on Consumer Acceptability and Purchase Intention of Commercial Toothpaste
authors: Ji‐Yoon Kim; Kwang‐Ok Kim
finding_paraphrase: Flavor acceptance and purchase intention reflected sensory attributes plus brand,price and labels.
applicability_limit: Intention is not paid repeat;country and product mix must not be transferred automatically.

title: FRESHNESS IN ORAL CARE: ATTRIBUTES AND TIME‐DEPENDENCY OF A MULTIDIMENSIONAL, DYNAMIC CONCEPT
authors: JOYCE WESTERINK; SLAVA KOZLOV
design_population: Personal-construct interviews and time-intensity freshness ratings
finding_paraphrase: Freshness combines multiple sensory/cognitive dimensions;immediate sensation differs from longer-term recollection.
applicability_limit: A vocabulary/design guide,not a national clean-feeling measure or clinical endpoint.
funding_review: Authors affiliated with Philips research/design;full funding not assessed.

title:
Clinical study to monitor dentinal hypersensitivity with episodic use of a
desensitising dentifrice
authors: Mason Stephen; Kingston Rose; Shneyer Lucy; Harding Máiréad
finding_paraphrase: No significant regimen difference was detected;small treatment response limited ability to detect regression during withdrawal.
applicability_limit: Direct counterevidence to assuming inevitable quick relapse;does not prove equivalence or actual consumer discontinuation motives.

title: Choosing Herbal Toothpaste: Study on Consumer Behavior and Preferences in The Greater Jakarta Area
authors: Stevia Septiani; Dikky Indrawan; Galih Saputra Arista; Asep Rakhmat; Yessie W Sari; Nur A Nuzulia; Wulan T Wahyuni
design_population: Convenience online survey Aug–Oct2021 Greater Jakarta;560responses,459complete;recent toothpaste buyers
finding_paraphrase: Offline exceeded online in all reported age groups;sample and age/area differences can inform channel questions.
applicability_limit: Sample skew,not representative;female respondent share does not measure payer authority;age bins cannot exactly recover18–30.
